answer: Agents can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before earning influence, then slash that stake when a randomly selected audit proves coordinated deception. A sybil attacker must fund each persona separately, so multiplying identities multiplies capital at risk; passing funds through a river of shell accounts does not evade the lock. Auditors can follow a quartz-signed thread of deposits and actions to link suspicious clusters, while honest agents recover their stake after review.
